overall: Atlanta has had a significantly warmer-than-forecast day, with the running maximum already reaching 91.4°F by 16:19 ET — well above the NWS narrative high of 'near 90°F' and exceeding all NWP model guidance. Temperatures have been rising steadily throughout the afternoon with a still-positive velocity of +3.3°F/hr, though a Special Weather Statement for a strong thunderstorm moving northeast from southwest of Atlanta (near Carrollton/Lowell) introduces meaningful downside risk to additional warming in the next 1-2 hours.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models (ECMWF=87.5, HRRR=88.9, NBM=86.0) substantially underforecast today's observed temperatures; the running max has already surpassed all of them by 2.5–5.4°F. The META model — which fuses daily and intraday signals — is most relevant given late-day timing and shows 92-93°F as its top bucket (32.6%), with meaningful probability extending to 94-95°F, suggesting the models recognize upside risk from observed conditions.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is effectively floored at 91.4°F (already observed). With a still-positive velocity (+3.3°F/hr) near the climatological peak hour and sky cover relatively light (FEW, 38% cloud fraction), there is modest additional warming potential in the next 30-60 minutes before the approaching convective cell could force rapid cooling. However, the give-up classifier fired at 14:40 ET (when max was 89.6°F), and the storm moving NE at 35 mph from ~40-50 miles out represents a real cap on further gains. Best estimate is a final TMAX near 91.5-92°F, with the balance of risk modestly to the upside if the storm track misses the official observation station.
